---
title: With an AI Assistant
---

An AI assistant that can run commands can check a package with pycmdcheck and
fix what the report names. pycmdcheck comes with a skill for that, which is a
short file of instructions the assistant loads when you ask for such a check.

## What an Assistant Gets

- A [JSON report](cli.qmd#json-output) in which every finding has a rule code
  and a hint. The code is a stable name, and the hint is one sentence that
  says what to do.
- A listing of every rule. `pycmdcheck --list-rules --json` prints each code
  with its hint, so an assistant can look a code up on its own.
- The [`triage` profile](triage.qmd), which only reads files. An assistant
  can start with it and run none of your code.

## Installing the Skill

Run this command in the root of a project. It copies the skill to
`.claude/skills/pycmdcheck`, where Claude Code looks for it.

```bash
pycmdcheck --install-skill
```

To use the skill in every project, name the skills directory in your home
directory.

```bash
pycmdcheck --install-skill ~/.claude/skills
```

Run the command again after you upgrade pycmdcheck, and it replaces the copy
with the skill of the new version. With `uvx pycmdcheck --install-skill`
nothing has to be installed first. The
[command-line reference](cli.qmd#install-skill) has the rules of the option.

In Claude Code 2.1.275 or later the skill can be installed as a plugin
instead. Type this line inside Claude Code.

```
/plugin install pycmdcheck --marketplace coatless-py-pkg/pycmdcheck
```

The plugin has the same version number as pycmdcheck, and an update of the
plugin brings the new skill when that number has changed. As a plugin the
skill is named `/pycmdcheck:pycmdcheck`. A copy in `.claude/skills` is named
`/pycmdcheck`.

An installed pycmdcheck also holds the skill inside the package, in
`.agents/skills/pycmdcheck`, which is where
[Library Skills](https://library-skills.io) looks. In a project that has
pycmdcheck in its environment, `uvx library-skills --claude` can link the
skill into `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`. The links follow the
installed version.

In the [repository](https://github.com/coatless-py-pkg/pycmdcheck) the skill
is the folder `skills/pycmdcheck`, which can also be copied by hand.

Then ask in your own words, for example "check this package" or "get this
package ready for a pyOpenSci review". The skill needs pycmdcheck 0.2.0 or
later, and it has the assistant check the version first. Its one file,
`SKILL.md`, follows the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format,
so an assistant that reads that format can load it from its own skills
directory. Name that directory after the option, as in
`pycmdcheck --install-skill .agents/skills`.

## What the Skill Does

The skill has the assistant work in this order.

1. Find pycmdcheck and check its version.
2. Run the `triage` profile and read the JSON report.
3. When you asked for fixes, fix one finding at a time, the most severe
   first, and run again to confirm that its code is gone. It corrects what is
   there, and asks before it adds something new.
4. Ask before it runs your code or your tools.
5. End with what it found, what it fixed, what is still open and why, which
   checks were skipped or have not run, and the questions that wait for you.

It tells the assistant to ask you before it does any of these. A request such
as "check this package" does not count as a yes.

- Run your tests, your doctests or your build, or start your linter, type
  checker or formatter. The build also downloads the build tools your project
  names.
- Run the `urls` check, which sends requests over the network.
- Add new content, such as a README, tests or a description. It can offer a
  draft from what your files show, and it writes the draft after a yes.
- Make a choice that is yours. That covers the license, a code of conduct, a
  contributing guide, a citation file, a changelog, CI, the build backend,
  the supported Python versions, how the package is installed, names, contact
  details and a version number.
- Install pycmdcheck with pip, create an environment, or install or configure
  a tool that a skipped check names. It may fetch pycmdcheck with `uvx` or
  `pipx run`, which changes none of your environments.

It also tells the assistant never to make a report pass by hiding a problem,
unless you ask for exactly that. That rules out a check that is switched off,
`--skip`, `# doctest: +SKIP` on an example that fails, a test or example
weakened only so that it passes, and a placeholder file added only to satisfy
a check. When a test disagrees with the code and your files do not show which
one is wrong, it asks you.

The skill approves no command ahead of time, so your assistant asks for
permission as it usually does. An assistant can still go against these
instructions, so read what it changed before you keep it.
